Hi Jordan / Rajiv —

Following up on Marissa’s notes with the benchmark highlights we ran against a workload that mirrors the numbers you gave on the call. Short summary below; full data attached (acme_latency_benchmarks.pdf) and a CSV matrix for different batch sizes (redwood_throughput_matrix.csv). Link to the shared report: https://redwood-share/benchmarks/acme-20260309

Environment: Redwood Dedicated-like config (single inference pod on 8xA100-equivalent), model: open-llama-13b-quant (representative), tokens/sample: median 150, max 512. 

Key numbers (representative):
- Median latency (no batching): ~40–60 ms for 256 tokens
- p95 latency (no batching): ~110–140 ms for 512 tokens
- With dynamic batching (agg batch ~8): throughput increases ~3–4x, effective token/sec per GPU ~12k–18k depending on sequence length
- Sustained concurrent RPS with autoscale policy: ~180–240 small requests/sec per pod (150 token avg); for your 200–400 concurrent users we recommend a 2–3 pod starting config with burst headroom

Notes: 
- Latency numbers are influenced by model architecture and kv cache usage; we can run a focused test on your exact prompt set if you want more precise numbers.
- We saw predictable improvements with quantized variants; we can include a model-variant cost/latency table in the SOW.

I attached the full report and a throughput CSV that breaks down p50/p95 across token lengths and batch sizes. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through any row of the CSV.

Cheers,
Dev

Attachments: acme_latency_benchmarks.pdf (3 pages summary), redwood_throughput_matrix.csv
